negative_findings.description: No public, enumerable registry of Bank iD RELYING PARTIES (poskytovatelé služeb / SeP) was located. Searches surfaced only the member-bank list, the implementation page, and scattered individual announcements; secondary sources explicitly advise checking the operator's own site for the current list, implying no downloadable roster.
negative_findings.result_summary: Bank member list recoverable (ČS, KB, ČSOB, Air Bank, MONETA, mBank, Raiffeisenbank, Fio); relying-party list not found as a structured public artefact.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The relying-party registry is the highest-value partnership pointer named in the cell rationale; without it, partnership intelligence must be reconstructed from press releases and the NIA qualified-provider list, which is slower and incomplete.

negative_findings.description: Czech-language searching for ČNB public procurement / supplier information for CERTIS and the instant-payment platform returned only scheme documentation, no tender notices, contract awards or supplier names.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search on 'ČNB veřejné zakázky CERTIS dodavatel' returned exclusively CERTIS rules and participant PDFs.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The identity of the technology supplier behind CERTIS/instant payments is a key vendor-intelligence fact; it likely requires the national procurement register (Věstník veřejných zakázek / NEN) rather than web search, which this pass did not reach.

negative_findings.description: The COBS rulebook PDF referenced by search results (cbaonline.cz/upload/1061-cobs-rulebook-v04-1-1.pdf) and references to later versions (v2, v6.0) could not be reconciled to a canonical version index; the ČBA landing page fetched exposed no version numbers, working groups or download links.
negative_findings.result_summary: ČBA open-banking page fetched successfully but contained only introductory text.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Without a canonical COBS version index we cannot date standard changes, which is the mechanism that links regulation to bank IT spend.

negative_findings.description: No search was run in Czech for CERTIS/instant-payments ISO 20022 migration terminology or for ČNB annual payment-system reports (Zpráva o platebním styku), so those sub-areas are undocumented in this slice.
negative_findings.result_summary: Sub-area left uncovered within the time budget.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: ISO 20022 migration and the annual payment-system report are standard triggers for bank infrastructure programmes.

coverage_gaps.description: Public-procurement sources are entirely absent from this slice: Věstník veřejných zakázek, NEN, TED (EU), and contract registers (Registr smluv) were not searched, yet they are where infrastructure supplier selections become public.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated pass over vestnikverejnychzakazek.cz, nen.nipez.cz, smlouvy.gov.cz and TED with CZ payments keywords (okamžité platby, platební systém, CERTIS, bankovní identita, API brána) and buyer=ČNB / state bodies.

coverage_gaps.description: Sector coverage is bank-centric; the cell's 'both' sector scope means non-bank payment infrastructure actors were under-covered — card scheme/ATM and switching operators active in CZ, and the CZ card-processing side generally.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Extend the actor map with CZ payment-processing and switching actors and search for their scheme membership and participant listings in both cs and en.

coverage_gaps.description: Most candidate URLs come from search-result metadata rather than direct fetches; only the ČBA open-banking page was fetched in this pass. Several deep-link PDFs and registry endpoints are therefore inferred, not observed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run the deterministic liveness pass over every URL and re-derive PDF links from their parent index pages rather than trusting search-result deep links.

coverage_gaps.description: Case studies are the weakest of the four topics here: infrastructure operators publish rules and rosters, not implementation narratives. Only bank press releases and trade media currently carry case-study material.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pair each infrastructure registry entry with a targeted vendor-side search (integrator reference pages, conference decks) for the named bank + scheme go-live date.

coverage_gaps.description: Slovak-language sources were not searched even though several CZ-market institutions (e.g. UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia) operate cross-border and publish SK-language infrastructure material.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add sk-language queries for shared CZ/SK entities where the Czech entity is a branch of a combined institution.

brief: Czech payment-infrastructure intelligence is unusually well served at the registry layer: ČNB publishes a version-numbered CERTIS instant-payment participant list and a versioned scheme rulebook, JERRS exposes the full licensed-PSP population through a documented web service, and pan-European registers (EPC Register of Participants, EBA CLEARING RT1/STEP2) cover the euro side. The standards layer sits with the Czech Banking Association, whose COBS open-banking rulebook is the specification every CZ integration vendor builds against, mirrored commercially by Trask's apiportal.cz and community bank-developer indexes. The identity layer — Bank iD (member banks: ČS, KB, ČSOB, Air Bank, MONETA, mBank, Raiffeisenbank, Fio) alongside CZ.NIC's mojeID, both hanging off the state NIA node — is the richest partnership pointer in the cell, but its relying-party roster is not published as a structured list, so partnerships must be reconstructed from bank press releases, the NIA qualified-provider register and critical trade coverage in Lupa.cz. The two largest holes are supplier identity (no procurement source searched: Věstník/NEN/Registr smluv/TED) and forward demand signalling around the July 2027 euro instant-payments obligation and the ECB digital euro rulebook, both of which deserve dedicated follow-up passes.
